title: Music in Manhattan: the studio orchestra instead of his band
summary: For this 1944 film he recorded with Mischa Bakaleinikoff's studio orchestra because he had no band at the time.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah, up to the time -- to and including the time when she married Axel Stordahl. 1296, "Music in Manhattan," 1944. You did a lot of films in '44, right? Comedy with music and a particularly tiresome plot. Features Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra.

Well, it wasn't my orchestra. It was the studio orchestra, because I had been having my jousts with the -- I went through induction seven times, you know, and everytime you figure, well, of course, this is it. And I was never in 4-F, and either they changed the laws or one time the guy decided I was a lush, but anyway, I finally decided I can't keep a band when I don't know what's going to happen. So I had come out to California. And I got this picture. Of course I didn't have a band, and they said, well, that's all right, we'll use the studio band. So we used the -- Bakaleinakoff was the director there, and he had a bunch of great guys in the band there at the studio, and I just used

part of them and recorded these things, and then they used a sideline group for the actual filming. I think it was Ann Shirley and Phillip Barry were in the picture. I have no idea what the picture was about.
It doesn't say here. Which Bakaleinikoff, Mischa or Constantine?
